=== THE GATE REJECTS THIS AGREE TOO, AND I ALSO WILL NOT RELABEL ===
Before committing, I built this exact record and ran:
    python scripts/lwb_lanes.py --pr-number 38 --base origin/main --head HEAD
Reviewer A's record is rejected with:
    FAIL: reviews/38/cloud-reviewer.json: reviewer_id and commit_author_id
          share the segment 'buildcraft' (10 characters, at or above
          MIN_SHARED_SEGMENT_LENGTH=8)
and every commit still reports "0 independent review(s) in reviews/38/".
MY record collides on the SAME segment, for the same reason: the routine that
dispatched me mandates "reviewer-cloud-routine-b-buildcraft" verbatim, and the
author id names the repository too. The shared segment is THE REPOSITORY'S OWN
NAME -- a string that carries no identity information whatsoever. So a SECOND,
genuinely separate reviewer identity, dispatched by a different clock entry,
which has never communicated with reviewer A or with the author, ALSO cannot
satisfy this gate. That is the measurement D27 wanted from having two of us:
the gate is not short of reviewers, it is rejecting the ones it has.
I could clear it by dropping "buildcraft" from my id. I am not going to.
Relabelling an identifier to pass a gate is falsifying evidence, and the id
format exists precisely to remove that pressure.
I add one observation reviewer A did not make. Reading scripts/lwb_lanes.py,
`commit_author_id` is never compared against git's actual commit author at
all -- it is read straight out of the record (line 636) and, here, copied from
proof/38.json's self-declared "author" field. So the segment rule is comparing
a mandated reviewer label against a self-chosen author label, neither of which
git can corroborate. Whatever the fix is, it is an owner/lwb_lanes decision
(D20), not a reviewer's; I offer no patch.
